tech.title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
tech.summary: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis is a weaker version of the Riemann hypothesis, arguably the biggest open question in math. Resolving the Riemann hypothesis would enable mathematicians to better understand the nature of prime numbers. OpenAI's recently released proof for the quasi-Riemann hypothesis is the most significant AI-for-math achievement so far, by quite a margin. The vast majority of the consequences of resolving it already follow from solving the quasi-Riemann hypothesis.

tech.title: Startup taps underwater volcano as energy source in “proof point” test
tech.summary: Endurance Energy, a Seattle-based startup, recently demonstrated the technical feasibility of using an active underwater volcano to generate electricity. The startup deployed a 3-ton prototype power plant at the Axial Seamount in the northeast Pacific Ocean in September and generated less than 10 seconds of net-positive electricity. The company's next trial run, planned for the winter of 2026 to 2027, will aim to sustain higher power generation. It is currently developing a 2-megawatt commercial generator for its first planned commercial deployment with the Kingdom of Tonga in 2027.

tech.title: Get 25% more from your training GPUs

tech.title: Introducing Clairic, a new System One class of extraction models
tech.summary: Clairic is an extraction model. Extraction models are a new class of System One-style models that can extract, compute, estimate, and forecast values from unstructured inputs, all at significantly higher accuracy, faster latency, and lower cost than traditional LLMs. It answers with values directly extracted from the input, computed from it, or predicted beyond it. The model can't produce a mistyped answer or hallucinate in the same way an LLM can, but it can still make mistakes.

tech.title: Cutting our inference bill by 68% by being obsessive about optimization

The biggest single saving came from checking what actually reached the provider on each session's first request, and finding a way to order those messages in a way that was as consistent as possible across commits, merge requests, and repositories. Check whether each session's first request actually reads from the cache and whether reviewers still find real problems at the effort level being paid for.

tech.title: AI will not automate radiologists like you think

This is similar to how programming is thriving despite drastic change in the field. It may be possible one day to use radiology images to predict disease probabilities far into the future. Any domain where demand can be elastic and quality can scale with increased intelligence will similarly flourish with the development of AI.

ai.title: Introducing Clairic, a new System One class of extraction models
ai.summary: Clairic can extract, compute, estimate, and forecast values from unstructured inputs. ai.title: AI Benchmarks: Climbing the Wrong Hills

webdev.title: When Retries Make Things Worse: Protecting Your System From Overload
webdev.summary: Retries can turn a slow dependency into a wider outage by multiplying attempts and exhausting connections or workers. A PHP example combines one retry owner, an operation deadline, admission limits, shared retry budgets, and jitter, then outlines a load test that measures both overload and recovery.

webdev.title: The generic circular dependency problem
webdev.summary: Generic services become coupled to their consumers when shared types or domain logic pull application knowledge back into analytics, email, or authorization modules. Domain wrappers, locally owned handlers, smaller contracts, and plugin registration can break those cycles, while extracting a shared type package may only hide the conceptual coupling.

webdev.title: Making a website AI friendly: what the bots actually fetched from mine
webdev.summary: An analysis of 18 days of traffic to one personal site found that verified crawlers mostly fetched ordinary pages, robots.txt, and the sitemap. Markdown copies attracted verified crawlers within a day, while llms.txt saw no verified training or search crawler requests, suggesting that basic HTML and measured traffic matter more than adding every proposed discovery file.

webdev.title: Writing is no longer proof of work
webdev.summary: Organizations often use reports and templates as evidence that someone put in effort, followed a process, or understood a topic. LLMs weaken that signal by producing plausible documents without the underlying work, leaving companies to find better evidence and reserve careful writing for actual communication.

webdev.title: No more tech debt

The team migrated through 45 pull requests across eight stacks, using vertical slices and before-and-after screenshots, then removed the old patterns so agents would stop copying them.

webdev.title: Developing Taste

infosec.title: CVE-2026-108082: Symfony ReDoS. One request. Seconds of CPU
infosec.summary: A crafted Cache-Control header triggers catastrophic regex backtracking in Symfony's HeaderUtils::split(). Symfony parses it on every request, before routing or authentication, and Laravel parses it three times. One request can consume up to 12.7 seconds of CPU, and four merged 8 KB headers can force timeouts. The flaw affects Symfony 4.1 through the October 2026 patches, including Laravel, Drupal, PrestaShop, and Shopware.

infosec.title: One Compromised Login Exposed Millions of California Students' Records
infosec.summary: An unauthorized party used a compromised login from May 22 to September 18 to copy California student files from an Educational Testing Service SFTP server. The data covers current and former students dating to 2006 and may include names, addresses, IDs, disability status, accommodations, and test results. The breach did not expose Social Security numbers, passwords, or financial details. ETS disabled the account, took the site offline, and is building a replacement system.

infosec.title: 2.76M Pieces of Customers' Info at Hollys Leaked in Cyberattack
infosec.summary: Korean coffee chain Hollys disclosed that it suffered a data breach impacting 2.76M pieces of personal information. The breached data includes dates of birth, phone numbers, addresses, and emails. The data was contained in temporary files provided for a past membership service overhaul.

infosec.title: Web Environment Integrity vs. Private Access Tokens - They're the same thing!
infosec.summary: Web Environment Integrity (WEI) and Apple's Private Access Tokens (PAT) both use signed browser or device attestations. A site can request proof that a visitor uses a genuine, non-jailbroken iPhone with Safari, then reject Firefox on Linux. WEI can additionally bind an attestation to a specific operation. The two proposals differ mainly in presentation: PAT is framed around fewer CAPTCHAs, while WEI is framed around service-provider verification.

infosec.title: PwnEscape: Guest-to-Host KVM Escape (CVE-2026-99999)
infosec.summary: Researchers found a Linux networking flaw that lets an untrusted VM guest alter IPv4 header bytes after the host kernel validates them. Guest-controlled checksum metadata can change the IPv4 header length, causing the kernel to copy 32 bytes beyond the packet's logical data and transmit them as apparent IP options. In a controlled KVM lab, the disclosure supported selected 64-byte host-kernel writes and execution of a host-root helper. The upstream fix, commit 6785011f8b16, validates checksum_start before checksum completion across five IPv4 consumers.

infosec.title: Managing Agentic Security at Scale
infosec.summary: Salesforce divides vulnerabilities into strategic and tactical vulnerabilities to address the large amount of vulnerabilities that are discovered by LLMs. Strategic vulnerabilities are vulnerabilities due to a core, systemic issue where many vulnerabilities can be resolved by fixing the core issue. Tactical vulnerabilities represent exploit chains that chain together smaller severity issues for a larger impact and require exploit verification in a staging environment.

The attackers used 4,630 gift cards totaling around $425K.

infosec.title: Plex vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild to drop a cryptominer

The observed source IPs were 45.194.92[.]222, 91.92.40[.]202, and 176.65.139[.]228, and the payload host was 217.60.194[.]116.

infosec.title: Anthropic Quietly Pitches its Own AI Safety Bill to Lawmakers

Independent evaluators would register with the Department of Commerce and report any such risk within 72 hours.

A simple system can keep chronological observations and evolving ideas in running notes while maintaining a separate dated decision log that records what is currently true without deleting previous decisions. AI makes large amounts of context searchable, but chronology and structure remain essential because a searchable mess is still a mess.

design.title: UX designers are not designing interfaces, they design personalities
design.summary: Digital products increasingly translate human behavior into metrics such as sleep scores, ratings, streaks, story points, and follower counts, which can gradually influence how people understand themselves and behave. These measurements expose only selected parts of reality, yet their apparent objectivity can give them greater authority than unmeasured experiences, relationships, and intuition. UX designers therefore shape more than interfaces and experiences: by deciding which metrics products emphasize, they influence how people perceive themselves and should deliberately leave room for realities that cannot be quantified.

design.title: A Web Framework for Building 3D/AR/VR Experiences
design.summary: Make 3D worlds with HTML and Entity-Component, on any headset, mobile, and desktop.

design.title: Fulham F.C gets a brand refresh built on hand-rendered lettering found on the walls of its stadium
design.summary: Fulham F.C's refreshed identity by Music and F37 Foundry is built around FFC Original, a bespoke typeface inspired by hand-rendered lettering discovered inside Craven Cottage, London's oldest football stadium. Rather than placing historical references alongside a contemporary identity, the system uses the club's physical heritage as the source of its modern visual language. The typography now extends across matchday graphics, campaigns, retail, moving image, and a 2026/27 away-kit campaign inspired by the visual language of the 1990s.

design.title: WCAG 3: A Different Future for Accessibility
design.summary: WCAG 3, still a draft, is the first ground-up rebuild of the standard since 1999, proposing to replace binary pass/fail with a graded model where meeting core requirements is a floor. Bronze, silver, and gold levels would let organizations be recognized for going further. Accessibility laws point to WCAG, so the change must keep regulators able to adopt it.

design.title: Structure First: The Inverted Pyramid and Visual Organization
design.summary: The inverted pyramid makes web content easier to consume by putting the essential message first and progressively adding supporting detail, ensuring readers understand the key point even if they stop early. Individual paragraphs should similarly lead with their main idea, while descriptive headings, short paragraphs, lists, and selective emphasis provide visual entry points for people scanning rather than reading linearly. A useful test is whether someone can understand something meaningful from a page within five seconds without reading its body copy. AI-generated writing is particularly worth checking for conclusions buried beneath unnecessary setup.

design.title: UX Maps: Glossary
design.summary: NN/g's UX Maps glossary defines and distinguishes common mapping tools.

design.title: At ORGATEC 2026 Sihoo Introduces Self Adjusting Chairs Built to Boost Creative Work
design.summary: Sihoo's self-adjusting H300 Pro and Doro C300 Pro V2 chairs, which have lumbar support that adapts to posture shifts, will be shown at ORGATEC 2026 in Cologne.

marketing.title: What if you could unboring your boring talking head videos?
marketing.summary: Your videos are about to get a serious glow-up. Meet Mochine by Wistia , a new way to turn boring talking-head videos into something worth watching. Ask Mochine to: Bring your videos to life with Motion Kits. Add eye-catching animated graphics that make your message stand out. Make it yours. Create custom Motion Kits that match your brand simply by pasting in your website URL. Fine-tune your edits. Trim clips and see every motion graphic on a new timeline right below your preview. Less time editing. More motion. A lot less boring. Try Mochine

marketing.title: How Consumer Desire for More Tactile, IRL Experiences Continues to Transform Marketing
marketing.summary: Gen Z is seeking offline experiences as digital fatigue grows, with 82% saying social media breaks improve their mental health and 70% planning to take up hands-on hobbies. Across the US, 75% see a simpler relationship with technology as a lifestyle upgrade. 68% collect physical items and 84% of Gen Z go out of their way for in-person shopping.

marketing.title: Half of Marketing Teams Are Replacing People With AI. Almost Nobody Can Prove It's Working
marketing.summary: Nearly 48% of marketing teams replaced human tasks with AI in the past year, but few can prove it works. A Basis survey found 65% of respondents either don't measure AI's return on investment or don't know if their organization does. Meanwhile, 51% expect substantial job losses across the industry within 3-5 years, even as AI's impact on marketing performance remains largely unproven.

marketing.title: Does AI drive more direct traffic?
marketing.summary: An analysis of 12 GA4 properties found no reliable evidence that AI-driven visits are hiding in Direct traffic. Total Direct sessions rose 141% from January to September, but engaged sessions stayed nearly flat due to bot traffic. Across 632 tests, AI visibility also showed no consistent link to subsequent branded search or Direct traffic. To measure AI's impact, track brand mentions across consistent prompts and platforms. Ask leads how they discovered you, then connect their responses to qualified leads, purchases, and revenue.

marketing.title: How A24 Made ‘You Can See Everything' a Must-See Film
marketing.summary: A24 had just 40 days to market its Elizabeth Holmes documentary, despite audiences already knowing the Theranos story from TV dramas and years of trial coverage. The campaign used cryptic teasers and provocative posters to make this version feel fresh. It built intrigue without spoiling the film's biggest surprises or making Holmes look like she was staging a comeback.

marketing.title: Your performance report knows Asset 18472 hit a 1.8% CTR. What was Asset 18472?
marketing.summary: Creative Data turns videos, images, and copy into structured information you and your agents can analyze. Discover why assets work and integrate that insight into briefs, media, brand governance, and AI workflows. Vidmob powers it with 40+ proprietary AI models and 25M+ creative assets. Explore Creative Analytics

marketing.title: Are you tracking the right prompts? (Webinar)
marketing.summary: Searchable is hosting a 60-minute working session on AI visibility tracking. They'll walk through how to map what buyers ask AI about your category, check where competitors win, and build your list of what to track next. The free webinar will take place today at 11 AM ET.

marketing.title: Journofinder
marketing.summary: Journofinder builds targeted media lists and secure press coverage. Its AI agent finds journalists with verified contact details, while its article search and real-time news alerts help PR teams identify timely pitching opportunities. It integrates with ChatGPT and Claude to streamline PR workflows.

marketing.title: Google Ads Now In AI Mode With Personal Intelligence
marketing.summary: Google is testing ads in AI Mode for users who enable Personal Intelligence by connecting apps like Gmail and Google Photos. While ads won't be based directly on inboxes or photo libraries, Google may use summaries and inferences from connected apps to personalize ad targeting. Advertisers won't have access to users' connected apps, and sensitive information won't be used to tailor ads.

marketing.title: Customer-centric thinking is too narrow
marketing.summary: Customer-centric marketing can overlook people who never buy but still influence how a market discovers and evaluates a brand. Journalists and practitioners shape public conversations and the information that search engines and AI systems use. Audience-centric marketing considers these groups when creating content and prioritizes resources that are easy to access, cite, and share. This can make ungated research and public documentation more valuable than lead-generation metrics suggest.

marketing.title: ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok chats reach trackers, study finds
marketing.summary: A study of 17 AI assistant experiences found that 8 shared conversation links, titles, or text with advertising and analytics firms. ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok all leaked shared chat links, while Grok also sent screenshots and prompts to Google, Meta, and TikTok. Rejecting cookies left 80.8% of trackers active, and 6 of 9 web assistants still contacted Google Ads. The findings highlight privacy risks for users discussing sensitive topics, even when AI providers offer training opt-outs.

marketing.title: Can social media bans protect young people's mental health?
marketing.summary: In Australia, 61% of children ages 12-15 still access banned platforms using false IDs or VPNs.

marketing.title: More Than Half of Podcast Listeners Say Ad Load Is Too High
marketing.summary: 55% of podcast listeners say there are too many ads, while host-read spots outperform prerecorded ads.

marketing.title: ‘No influencers': the hotels, restaurants and beauty spots restricting photoshoots
marketing.summary: Hotels and restaurants are restricting photography as visitors use them as content backdrops rather than places to eat or stay.

crypto.title: Revolut secures Gibraltar crypto licence to support international expansion plans
crypto.summary: Revolut got a Distributed Ledger Technology provider licence from the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission for a new entity, Revolut Global Digital Assets Limited. The entity will support its international crypto operations, alongside its existing UK and EEA (MiCA) entities. Revolut says it has over 80M retail customers and over 16M crypto users. It did not say which markets the Gibraltar entity will serve or when. Other recent moves are conditional OCC approval for a US bank charter last month and the euro stablecoin EURR rolling out in Denmark, Poland, and Portugal since August.

crypto.title: JPMorgan expands ‘JPM Coin' deposit token to Ethereum
crypto.summary: JPMorgan's Kinexys brought its USD deposit token JPM Coin (JPMD) to Ethereum for institutional clients. JPMD launched on Base in November 2025 and now supports peer-to-peer transfers across the EVM ecosystem, including Base and Ethereum. It represents existing JPMorgan bank deposits on a public chain. Kinexys says it has handled over $4T in cumulative transactions, averaging $7B a day. The bank launched a tokenized money-market fund on Ethereum in December and a second in May.

crypto.title: World launches World ID suite for banks
crypto.summary: World, co-founded by Sam Altman, launched a bank-focused World ID bundle at Money20/20. It combines the World ID app, World ID for Zoom (deepfake detection, now generally available after an April beta), and World ID for Agents (AgentKit, which lets a person delegate Proofs to an AI agent). World did not name a bank using it or give pricing. It says over 18M people hold a Proof of Human.

crypto.title: Stripe Link Agent Wallet v0.27.5
crypto.summary: Stripe released Link Agent Wallet v0.27.5 with two updates: expanded purchase-type coverage across hotels, flights, subscriptions, and recurring billing alongside standard ecommerce, and multi-currency support for hundreds of Stripe-supported currencies paired with geographic rollout to roughly six new markets beyond the US and Canada this month. The wallet abstracts card types, tokens, and payment protocols from agent code, letting agents submit spend requests without handling payment-type differentiation. The updates extend Link's reach from US-centric, single-purchase ecommerce to multi-leg travel, recurring billing, and cross-border transactions across a growing set of geographies.

crypto.title: The $280M Cost of Onboarding Retail to Hyperliquid
crypto.summary: A study of nearly 400,000 wallets trading Hyperliquid perpetuals through six consumer apps found cumulative losses of $280M all-time, with $126M accruing since November 2025. Fees drove slightly more than half those recent losses: builder fees stacked on Hyperliquid's base rate push per-$100 order costs to 6.5-14.5 cents, and small accounts turning over their balance many times compound those costs fast. Invo users show the extreme: $12.4M deposited against $5.8B traded, and on BTC positions, fee drag alone exceeded net gains from closed trades. Retention is poor across all six apps: about half of each month's active traders are first-timers, and only one in seven new traders remains active three months later, meaning growth has come from continuous new-user acquisition rather than building a durable base.

crypto.title: ETH is Ethereum's Most Important Application
crypto.summary: Gnosis is live with Ethereum's Fast Confirmation Rule (FCR), cutting L1-to-Gnosis deposit times from ~14 minutes to 12-24 seconds, with most consensus clients now shipping FCR behind an opt-in flag. AI agents completed formal verification of the FCR in Lean in 4-5 days, a task that used to take months, and the process caught a subtle fork-choice bug in the spec itself. A Cambridge workshop of 100+ researchers from 70 organizations advanced post-quantum cryptography and fast finality work, with Barnabé presenting a path to finality in tens of seconds in the I* fork after Hegotá, down from the current ~15 minutes. Quick Slots (EIP-8198) joined heze-devnet-2 alongside FOCIL, and Glamsterdam arrives on the Hoodi testnet on October 26.

crypto.title: Singapore Gulf Bank Enables Native USDT/USDC Conversion
crypto.summary: Singapore Gulf Bank, backed by Singapore's Whampoa Group, now lets retail customers convert between USD and USDT or USDC natively within its mobile banking app, eliminating the need to route funds through a separate crypto exchange. USD, USDT, and USDC sit in the same account, with conversions available around the clock Monday through Friday. SGB represents a growing class of Asia-based banks building stablecoin access directly into core banking infrastructure.

crypto.title: Stablecoin supply stalls, but payments jump 45% as Visa, Mastercard and Stripe connect crypto to cash
crypto.summary: Stablecoin payment volume hit $482 billion through September 2026, a 45% year-over-year gain, while total supply held flat at $305 billion, pointing to rising velocity rather than new issuance. Card spending linked to stablecoins reached $3.9 billion, roughly 10x the prior year, with sub-$50 purchases driving 84% of transaction count growth. Mastercard deployed its BVNK-built Global Money Platform combining fiat accounts, stablecoin balances, and card spending with Nuvei and Marqeta as first customers; Stripe is expanding stablecoin card coverage from 30 to 100-plus countries via a partnership with Plasma; and Visa's Inyo Global became the first commercial user of Visa Direct's USDC prefunding service for cross-border settlement. Stablecoin card spending still totals roughly 0.03% of Visa's $4 trillion quarterly payment volume, marking the distance between infrastructure buildout and adoption scale.

crypto.title: Big Q3 for Stacks
crypto.summary: Summary of Stacks' Q3 ecosystem report.

crypto.title: Crypto.com, Novig sue Missouri over sports event contracts; Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood hold off
crypto.summary: Missouri's attorney general sent cease-and-desist letters to six companies in mid-September.

crypto.title: BNB Chain burns 1.65M BNB worth about $1B in 37th quarterly auto-burn
crypto.summary: BNB Chain burned about 1.646M BNB, ~$1B at the reference price.

crypto.title: Turnkey Console Launch
crypto.summary: Turnkey launched Console, an operator dashboard that consolidates fund sends and receives, asset swaps, balance monitoring, transaction approvals, wallet creation, and policy configuration into a single interface for teams running onchain businesses.

it.title: Accenture weighs $1.5 billion sale of its China consulting business
it.summary: Accenture has hired JPMorgan to explore the sale of its Greater China consulting operations in a deal potentially worth up to $1.5 billion. The strategic review follows unsolicited interest and comes as Beijing restricts foreign consultants from advising state-owned enterprises. Meanwhile, Accenture is redirecting capital and focus toward expanding its artificial intelligence capabilities globally.

it.title: OpenAI reports major gains in legacy-code modernization
it.summary: OpenAI introduced evaluations for building software across 20 programming languages and migrating COBOL while preserving behavior. On its COBOL migration benchmark, GPT-6.1 Sol reached 86.6% accuracy at low reasoning effort, compared with 5.4% for GPT-5.6 Sol, suggesting progress on maintaining and modernizing legacy enterprise systems.

it.title: Microsoft exits UK data center deal amid power delays
it.summary: Microsoft reportedly terminated its agreement for capacity at Nscale's planned Loughton facility amid electricity supply delays that could extend into the 2030s. Nscale says the development will proceed and its other Microsoft contracts remain unaffected, highlighting the growing importance of power availability in AI infrastructure planning.

it.title: Enterprise AI outcomes depend on the art of unlearning
it.summary: Enterprise AI adoption often falls short because organizations overlook the human element of change management. Successful digital transformation in the agentic era requires empowering employees to unlearn old software habits, supported by dedicated roles like Forward Deployed Engineers and Agentic Design Leads.

it.title: Enterprise AI needs runtime governance and better context
it.summary: Scaling enterprise AI requires coordinating what agents know with what they are permitted to do. Runtime access controls, audit trails, retrieval, and memory need to work together as agents operate across enterprise systems.

it.title: The agents nobody meant to build
it.summary: IT leaders face an emerging challenge with unsanctioned AI agents created inadvertently by employees using approved desktop tools and recurring workflows. Gartner forecasts that 40% of enterprises will demote or shut down agents by 2027 due to governance gaps, security risks, and a lack of ownership visibility. Managing this risk requires placing hard limits on what agents can touch and integrating education directly into tool access.

it.title: Cloudflare expands enterprise integrations for its AI workspace
it.summary: Cloudflare expanded the partner ecosystem for Cloudflare OS with integrations spanning Asana, Box, Canva, ClickHouse, GitHub, Gong, and Notion. The announcement also adds professional services partners to help enterprises train employees and adopt AI workflows connected to their existing tools.

it.title: Lenovo's AI Express targets enterprises waiting for AI servers
it.summary: Lenovo's AI Express is a quick-ship programme developed with Nvidia that aims to cut enterprise AI server lead times to as little as 15 business days. The offering provides three pre-validated configurations ranging from small inference setups to large generative AI platforms using Blackwell hardware. The program is designed for enterprises struggling with hardware scarcity. Orders are subject to strict caps and eligibility checks.

it.title: Cisco Secure Email Gateway Zero-Day Exploited Again
it.summary: Cisco confirmed that a zero-day vulnerability in its Secure Email Gateway, tracked as CVE-2026-76519 with a CVSS score of 9.8, is actively being exploited in the wild. The path traversal flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to write files and execute root-level commands via crafted email attachments when File Reputation is enabled. Security agencies, including CISA and Germany's BSI, have issued warnings and urgent patching deadlines.

it.title: Why GPU Cloud Observability Is Harder Than It Looks
it.summary: GPU cloud observability requires connecting physical infrastructure topology with active workloads, yet traditional monitoring tools often remain isolated by subsystem. Building a live, topology-aware model enables operators to trace performance bottlenecks, manage capacity fragmentation, and correlate hardware telemetry with distributed training or inference jobs.

it.title: OpenCode reports account compromise
it.summary: Attackers compromised an older OpenCode system, affecting 1.4% of Console users.

it.title: IBM Doesn't Need to Sell More Products, It Needs to Sell Its Enterprise AI Harness
it.summary: IBM successfully scaled an internal AI harness built over two and a half years to a significant portion of its client base, demonstrating a viable business model for enterprise transformation.
